Replaced the brittle resolver with an explicit-override -> PATH -> validated-installed-bin resolver (candidate must pass --version; highest validated version wins deterministically), verified against bin/80f78947ad880e6e/codex.exe v0.155.0-alpha.16.3. Auth confirmed locally via `codex doctor --json` (auth configured, storage mode File, auth mode chatgpt, stored API key false); no token or credential value was read, logged, or committed. A harmless, deterministic, non-interactive `codex exec --json` smoke through the existing E3 adapter returned READY (exit 0, thread 01a0cffb-4ca1-7052-babc-3db7a233ddac, ~6.0s, safe workspace-write profile). Provider `openai` is deterministically reported, but the served model is not exposed (server model present=false), so execution model identity stays UNKNOWN; local config's gpt-6-astra is recorded only as configured_model. Provider usage IS exposed on the CLI's turn.completed event (16207 in / 13184 cached / 5 out); the E2 row was written before the extractor fix was verified, so its token columns are null (documented, not hidden, and no extra request was spent to correct it). E2 linkage VERIFIED via the public governor.record_request() interface as obs-20260923-d42e34a5. routable=true, qualification UNPROVEN, E3 Stage 2 untouched. Two further genuine adapter defects were found and fixed from real evidence: the assistant reply arrives as an item.completed item of type `agent_message` (not `message`), and boolean fields in `doctor --json` are strings. Full regressions: 271 collected / 271 passed / 0 errors across 7 suites (E3 baseline improved from 50/48/2 errors to 54/54/0). Two Codex executions were spent, not one, and both are disclosed in the repo records: the first proved execution worked while exposing our own parser defect, and the second produced the canonical PASS evidence.
